thread: The granary tally-man sends the party to Captain Havel at the market-gate militia post

evidence.clue: A man on foot walking out of Andorhal, ledger satchel at his hip, a pale stripe worn across his coat, ink on one cuff. Sylvanas stops him. He says he came 'this noon'. Asked who runs the granaries: 'Depends who you ask. The factors say it's the factors, the corn guild says the guild, the town says the town, and all three will sit you on a bench in the hall till they light the lamps.'

He recommends Captain Havel, militia: keep straight on at the bottom of the hill (the carts bear left to the yards) to the market gate; the militia post is just inside it on the left with a bench outside the door. 'He knows the granary district better than anybody. Better than the factors do, and they'd sooner not hear it.'

He looks back over his shoulder toward the granaries while answering (nothing to see but the rise and the dust), and looks over the four riders when stopped: bows, tall horses, Cyndia's hand near her quiver, the staff.
He says the farewell and is gone in the traffic before Sylvanas looks back. Jaina read nothing but the road's drag off him.

Chapter 7: the referral is a plain fact. Jaina names the tally-man to Havel ('A man on the road, a tally-man from the granaries, told us to ask here for Captain Havel'); Havel: 'You've found him. They do send them to me. I'm cheaper than a factor, and I'm still here after dark.' Sylvanas does not link the farewell to Havel.

Chapter 7: Havel is on the page as a harried, territorial, city-first captain. His information is real. Low-key plants (see thread havel-steers-the-lanes): Corin's notices unread under the river stone; the Hurdle Lane route 'so it's covered'; pointing past Tenter Row twice; 'Kett shut his gate at noon'; the same chalk line redrawn.

readerKnows_chapter7: Havel is helpful, slow and steers the lanes; Kett's turned out to be a live site he had said was shut. Nobody narrates him as cult-paid.
povCharacterKnows_chapter7: Sylvanas: wrong note with a documented bias beside it. She does not connect Havel to the tally-man or to the farewell.
readerKnows: The party has one name inside Andorhal; the man who gave it to them used the Millhaven farewell.
povCharacterKnows: Jaina: a tired clerk gave honest directions. Sylvanas: wrong note, no proof. The party knows Havel only as a militia captain who knows the granary district.
notes: The verified plan treats Havel as a figure the outline makes cult-paid in Ch7-8 and the tally-man as a plant who routes the party to him; per the prose, no character knows or suspects that and the narration does not tilt. Keep it an observable plant only.
